The Journey

Evolution of Artificial Intelligence

From theoretical concepts to transformative reality — trace the milestones that shaped our AI-powered world.

1950

The Turing Test

Alan Turing publishes "Computing Machinery and Intelligence," proposing the question: "Can machines think?" This foundational paper sets the stage for all of AI.

1956

Birth of AI

The Dartmouth Conference coins the term "Artificial Intelligence." John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, and others ignite a field that would change civilization forever.

1997

Deep Blue

IBM's Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov, proving machines could master complex strategic thinking beyond human expectations.

2012

Deep Learning Revolution

Geoffrey Hinton's AlexNet shatters ImageNet benchmarks, sparking the deep learning revolution that powers modern AI systems.

2017

Transformer Architecture

"Attention Is All You Need" introduces the Transformer, the architecture behind every modern large language model and the foundation of the AI we know today.

2023

The Generative AI Era

Large language models and generative AI reshape industries, creativity, and human-computer interaction. The age of intelligent assistants begins.

2025

AGI on the Horizon

Multi-modal models, reasoning agents, and autonomous systems push toward artificial general intelligence. The boundary between human and machine intelligence blurs.

What AI Can Do

Modern AI Capabilities

Explore the vast domains where artificial intelligence is transforming the world.

Natural Language

Understanding, generating, and translating human language with nuance, context, and creative expression.

Computer Vision

Seeing and interpreting visual data — from medical imaging to autonomous navigation and real-time object detection.

Reasoning

Logical deduction, mathematical problem-solving, and multi-step reasoning that approaches human-level analytical thinking.

Creative Generation

Generating art, music, code, and writing with originality and style that rivals human creative output.

Autonomous Agents

Self-directed AI systems that plan, execute, and adapt to accomplish complex goals with minimal human oversight.

Scientific Discovery

Accelerating research in biology, physics, and medicine by simulating experiments and generating novel hypotheses.
